findings.title: Q1 matches literally and misses recognized variants of Revenue operations
findings.observation: Rule Q1 matches only 'Revenue Operations Manager'. The knowledge base records 3 equivalent term(s) for Revenue operations that the rule does not recognize.

source_refs.text: 7 years as Revenue Operations Manager (by job title).

evidence.text: recognized variant(s): Revenue operations, RevOps, revenue ops

limitations: Synonyms improve recognition; they do not establish competence.
Terminology only; scope of revenue operations roles varies by organization.
Closely related (not equivalent) terms not proposed: commercial operations, sales operations, sales ops. Verify case by case.
findings.proposed_action: Add recognized variants to the rule: Revenue operations, RevOps, revenue ops.
findings.expected_benefit: Applicants describing the same work in different words are no longer filtered out.
findings.tradeoffs: Ambiguous abbreviations can admit unrelated profiles; review ambiguity notes first.

findings.title: Q1 counts experience only under specific job titles
findings.observation: Rule Q1 only counts experience held under the titles 'Revenue Operations Manager'. The underlying capability can be demonstrated under other titles and in other domains.

source_refs.text: 7 years as Revenue Operations Manager (by job title).

evidence.text: 7 years as Revenue Operations Manager (by job title).

limitations: Whether alternative experience is equivalent must be judged by a recruiter or hiring manager.
Title-based counting may reflect a deliberate employer choice; confirm intent.
findings.proposed_action: Count relevant experience by responsibilities, not titles: match recognized terminology across the full résumé and route equivalency evidence to recruiter review.
findings.expected_benefit: Candidates whose titles differ from the conventional path reach human review.
findings.tradeoffs: Responsibility-based matching needs recruiter verification; expect modest extra review time.
